source.title: Event recognition
source.abstract: Earlier work used hidden Markov models. We use a conditional random field with lexical features and semantic role features for event recognition. Our system achieves an F1 of 81% in event recognition.

contribution.concept: Our system achieves an F1 of 81% in event recognition

contrast: hidden Markov models is background; F1 is a metric, not a method. Keep the three used components separate. Using an existing technique does not make it a new artifact.

source.title: Image retrieval with ORBIT
source.abstract: We introduce ORBIT, a retrieval model. We use ORBIT and nearest-neighbor search for image retrieval. We evaluate on NorthSet and WestSet.

contrast: ORBIT can be both method and contribution. Evaluation on a resource is not itself a reported finding. NorthSet is not a method, and using nearest-neighbor search does not claim its invention.

source.title: Speech recognition with feature projection
source.abstract: We use feature projection for speech recognition. For Tamil, when test data exceeds training data, our model improves word accuracy by 5%. For Tamil, our model does not improve BLEU compared with the word-based baseline.

contribution.concept: For Tamil, when test data exceeds training data, our model improves word accuracy by 5%
For Tamil, our model does not improve BLEU compared with the word-based baseline

contrast: Tamil is a language, not a dataset name. Keep the leading condition, 5%, and the separate negative comparison. Do not label the comparison baseline as a method of this work. The new negative finding is not a motivating problem.
